function ScoringFunctions_Gatherer(aiPlayer)
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player)
	local villager_max_percentage = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_max_pop_percentage")
	local villager_production_delay_time = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_production_delay_time")  -- delay time between each villager queued up
	
	-- for naval maps, lower the max number of Villagers to make room for fishing boats
	if AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() and AI_AreThereAnyDeepwaterFish(aiPlayer) then
		if difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
		elseif difficulty == AID_HARD then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.05
		end
	end
	
	-- if super late into the game and higher difficulties, reduce the villagers to allow more room for traders and military 
	if World_GetGameTime() >= 60*40 and difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
		villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
	end
	
	local result = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_MultipleProduced(aiPlayer, 0.1),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxPopCapPercentage(aiPlayer, villager_max_percentage, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 3.0, 2.0, true, true)
	}
	
	-- if playing as Mongol or Golden Horde and higher difficulties
	if difficulty >= AID_HARD and Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		
		-- increase the production delay time to ensure that we have resources to age up to feudal age
		local DarkAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
			{
				AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, DarkAgeScoring),
				AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 55.5)
			})
		
		-- use default otherwise
		local feudal_age_list = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FeudalAgeScoring)
		}
		
		if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 then
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
		else
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 0.125)
		end
		
		local FeudalAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, feudal_age_list)
		
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {DarkAgeMinimumScoring, FeudalAgeMinimumScoring})
	end
	
	-- If the delay time is high enough, add the function to delay production.
	-- We need to check this because if the delay time is not greater than 0.125 seconds (one sim tick) then this scoring function throws an assert.  
	if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 and not Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") or AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "templar") then
		-- Templars use upgrades from the TC to age up, and this can be blocked by the villager production.
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NoUpgradeProductionBlockedByThisProduction(aiPlayer, "age_up_upgrade");
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_MilitaryProductionBuilding(aiPlayer)
	-- Buildings that produce military units or upgrades
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player) 
	local groupUtility = function(aiPlayer, pbg, prodGroupID)
		local perPBGCurrentScale = 0.25
		local perPBGEverScale = 0
		local maxPBGsFromGroupCurrent = -1
		return GroupUtility(aiPlayer, prodGroupID, pbg, maxPBGsFromGroupCurrent, perPBGCurrentScale, perPBGEverScale)
	end

	local result =  
	{
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, -1.0),
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["combat"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_ProductionQueueContention(aiPlayer, 8, 20),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, groupUtility),
		AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 10.0),
	}
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if difficulty <= AID_EASY then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, false)
	elseif difficulty == AID_NORMAL then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, -1, false)
	elseif difficulty >= AID_HARD then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, false)
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_DropOffs(aiPlayer)
	-- failsafe case makes the score for this dropoff very high if we have not recently 
	-- built a dropoff of this type AND the resource is fundamental (needed for building the dropoff) 
	-- AND we currently have very little of the resource
	local failsafe = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),
			
			-- returns a value between 0 and 1
			AIProductionScoring_AmountOfResourceNeeded(aiPlayer, 25.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_LowResourceIncome(aiPlayer, 4.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_IsProductionBlockedByThisResource(aiPlayer)
		})
	
	local normalDropoffScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			
			-- Do I need more drop offs go get the resources that I need/want (faster)?
			-- This is what drives the decision most of the time.
			-- 0 as long as we don't need the drop off at all.
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),

			-- When produced, pause production for some time, to let various parts of the AI react to the new drop off.
			-- Should not be too short because villagers need to walk to the construction site and build it before
			-- any of the other parts of AI (like ScarcityAndDeficiency) can update to the new dropoff being there.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 50.0),

			-- Return 0.0 if placement score is invalid, otherwise return 1.0, elephants should not come through this path
			AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScoreValid(aiPlayer),

			-- As of writing this comment we never drop economy all the way to 0 so this is just used to help order
			-- the queue based on strategic intention.
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		})
	
	-- if villagers run out of things to gather on colonized island it's better to try and build a dropoff then stand around doing nothing
	-- returns 0 or 1
	local villagersRunOutOfThingToGather = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
		{
			-- This is here because we can't figure out why the AI is sometimes going ham with lumber camps.
			-- At the time of adding this comment both other options have NotProducedRecently for at least 60s in the
			-- scoring, yet the AI can sometimes get into a bugged state where it is spamming down lumber camps in a
			-- 20 second interval. So the NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland probably has some edge
			-- case bug and can't be trusted. I'm forcing a 3 minute delay on this for the following reasons:
			-- 1. We don't have a good way to reproduce this bug.
			-- 2. This branch is meant to deal with naval maps where the AI colonizes new islands and needs to build
			--    drop-offs there. Naval AI has been de-prioritized and is less important than land features.
			--    This interferes with gameplay on land.
			-- 3. The worst case on a naval map would be that the AI just build a drop off before setting foot on a new
			--    island and has to wait for 3 minutes. But that is only the case if the normal drop off scoring branch
			--    doesn't trigger. If the normal scoring doesn't trigger then the AI doesn't need wood right now so no
			--    big loss. Just some idle villagers in edge case situations of a non-priority feature (naval).
			--    In contrast our current bad case is that the AI wastes all of it's wood in plastering the entire area
			--    in and around a forest with lumber camps. It wastes a lot of wood and wastes villager time by
			--    dedicating one to building more and more lumber camps. And the community called it out a lot.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),

			AIProductionScoring_NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland(aiPlayer)
		})
		
	return 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {normalDropoffScoring, failsafe, villagersRunOutOfThingToGather})		
	}
end

function ScoringFunctions_ResourceGenerator(aiPlayer)
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player) 
	
	local normalResourceGeneratorScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_ShouldNotConsiderNaval(aiPlayer, false),
			
			AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),
			AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 6*60),	-- only start scoring higher if game time is long enough
			AIProductionScoring_IncreaseOverTime(aiPlayer, 6*60, 5) -- increase score as time progresses after the 6 minute mark
		})
	
	-- scoring for minimum amount for naval ------------------------
	
	local navalResourceGeneratorScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_ShouldConsiderNaval(aiPlayer),
			
			-- AI-TODO: do we need a new resource deficiency scoring function?
			-- Note that we have a resource deficiency scoring function for dropoffs, which uses the resource that the 
			-- dropoff collects. We need a version that works with the resource that is produced by the generator. 
			-- (Although the ResourceGeneratorScore is based on the gathering requirements, which should be higher if 
		    -- the resource is scarce.)
			AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),
			AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 18, 18, false),
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
			AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 6*60),	-- only start scoring if game time is long enough
			AIProductionScoring_IncreaseOverTime(aiPlayer, 12*60, 1)
		})
	
	
	-- scoring for minimum amount for feudal age ------------------------
	
	local DarkAgeMinimumScoring = nil
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "english") and difficulty > AID_HARD then
		-- English want farms early
		DarkAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
			{
				
				-- When in Feudal Age, make sure you have a minimum number
				AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 2*60),
				AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, -1, false),
				AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
				AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0})
			})
	else
		-- none in feudal age
		DarkAgeMinimumScoring =  AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, alwaysReturnZero)
	end
	
	
	-- scoring for minimum amount for feudal age ---------------------
	
	local fuedal_list = 
		{
			
			-- When in Feudal Age, make sure you have a minimum number
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FeudalAgeScoring),
			AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
			AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 9*60)	-- only start scoring if game time is long enough
		}
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "english") and difficulty > AID_HARD then
		-- English wants more farms early, but we also want the english to scale it further up a little later in feudal age
		local early_feudal_score = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 6, -1, false)
		local late_feudal_list = {
			AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 12, -1, false),
			AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 13*60)	-- later than initial feudal age timing
		}
		local late_feudal_score = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, late_feudal_list)
			
		fuedal_list[#fuedal_list + 1 ] = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {early_feudal_score, late_feudal_score})
	else
		fuedal_list[#fuedal_list + 1 ] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, -1, false)
	end
	
	local FeudalAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, fuedal_list)
	
	

	-- scoring for minimum amount for castle age ------------------------
	
	local castle_list = nil
	local CastleAgeMinimumScoring = nil
	
	if difficulty > AID_HARD then
		castle_list = 
		{
			-- When in Castle Age, make sure you have a minimum number
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, CastleAgeScoring),
			AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 16*60),
			AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0})
		}
		
		-- Minimum number of resource generators
		if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "english") then
			-- english want more farms early
			castle_list[#castle_list + 1 ] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 24, -1, false)
		else
			castle_list[#castle_list + 1 ] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 16, -1, false)
		end
		
		CastleAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, castle_list)
	else
		CastleAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, alwaysReturnZero)
	end

		return 
		{

			AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 0.06, 2.0, true,true),
			AIProductionScoring_MaxPopCapPercentage(aiPlayer, 0.06, true),
			AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		}
	elseif Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer,'hre') then
		-- Boost the monk weight above villagers when we have less than 2 monks
		local urgentRatio = 1.4
		-- bump the score higher if we're past dark age
		if Player_HasUpgrade(player, BP_GetUpgradeBlueprint("feudal_age")) then
			urgentRatio = 3.0
		end
		
		function urgentPurposeWeight(aiplayer, pbg)
			return urgentRatio
		end
		
		-- when less than 2 monks are available they are very important to build
		local urgentScoreList = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, -1, true),
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, urgentPurposeWeight)
		}
		-- normal scoring
		local normalScoreList = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 0.5, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, {["religion"] = 1.0})),
			AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 0.06, 2.0, true,true)

		return

			branchingDecisions,
		}
	elseif Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, 'sultanate_ha_tug') then

function ScoringFunctions_Gatherer(aiPlayer)
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player)
	local villager_max_percentage = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_max_pop_percentage")
	local villager_production_delay_time = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_production_delay_time")  -- delay time between each villager queued up
	
	-- for naval maps, lower the max number of Villagers to make room for fishing boats
	if AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() and AI_AreThereAnyDeepwaterFish(aiPlayer) then
		if difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
		elseif difficulty == AID_HARD then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.05
		end
	end
	
	-- if super late into the game and higher difficulties, reduce the villagers to allow more room for traders and military 
	if World_GetGameTime() >= 60*40 and difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
		villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
	end
	
	local result = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_MultipleProduced(aiPlayer, 0.1),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxPopCapPercentage(aiPlayer, villager_max_percentage, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 3.0, 2.0, true, true)
	}
	
	-- if playing as Mongol or Golden Horde and higher difficulties
	if difficulty >= AID_HARD and Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		
		-- increase the production delay time to ensure that we have resources to age up to feudal age
		local DarkAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
			{
				AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, DarkAgeScoring),
				AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 55.5)
			})
		
		-- use default otherwise
		local feudal_age_list = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FeudalAgeScoring)
		}
		
		if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 then
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
		else
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 0.125)
		end
		
		local FeudalAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, feudal_age_list)
		
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {DarkAgeMinimumScoring, FeudalAgeMinimumScoring})
	end
	
	-- If the delay time is high enough, add the function to delay production.
	-- We need to check this because if the delay time is not greater than 0.125 seconds (one sim tick) then this scoring function throws an assert.  
	if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 and not Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") or AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "templar") then
		-- Templars use upgrades from the TC to age up, and this can be blocked by the villager production.
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NoUpgradeProductionBlockedByThisProduction(aiPlayer, "age_up_upgrade");
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_ExpansionTC(aiPlayer)
	
	function typicalPurposeWeight(aiplayer, pbg)
	   return 0.1
	end
	
	
	local expansionDecisionList = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, typicalPurposeWeight),
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true)
	}

	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		-- Typically Expansion TCs  placement style 'ExpansionBase' makes them build at
		-- suitable expansion sites (good resources). This in turn causes PlannedPlacementScore to
		-- modulate how many TCs we build.
		-- However all mongol structures use the build style 'NearBlueprint' which causes them
		-- to build near the ovoo. With this in mind PlannedPlacementScore will always be positive
		-- causing the Mongol AIPlayer to spam TCs. Therfore we must limit mongol TCs

		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true)
	else
		-- don't build more than 4 TCs. 3 + capital
		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	end
	
	local expansionDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,expansionDecisionList)
	
	local twoTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, TwoTCDesire),

		-- 1 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 2 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, 2, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local threeTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, ThreeTCDesire),

		-- 2 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 3 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, 3, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local islandDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_IslandNeedingExpansionBase(aiPlayer)
	
	-- We consider both possibilities and chose the max score
	local branchingDecisions = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		twoTCDesireBranch,
		threeTCDesireBranch,
		expansionDecisionBranch,
		islandDecisionBranch
	})
	
	local result =  
	{
		branchingDecisions,
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, 0.3),
	}
	
	return result
end

	-- At the start of the game we want an early cow, then we only want a few until we start having ranches to fill. As we get more ranches, then we increase cattle production.
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	
	-- this scoring function returns 0 if the game time is past a minimum duration
	function FirstCattleScoring(aiplayer) 
		if World_GetGameTime() < 6*60 then	
			return 0.0
		else
			return 1000.0
		end
	end
	
	-- scoring for the first cattle to produce at start of game
	local StartOfGameScoring = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FirstCattleScoring)
	}
	
	-- Scoring for low production of cows
	local MaintainSomeCows = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	
	-- Scoring for high production of cows. Requires a mill to prevent choking the town center villager production.
	local RanchProductionList =
	{
		AIProductionScoring_PresenceOfMyTypes(aiPlayer, {["villager"] = 0.01}, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PresenceOfMyTypes(aiPlayer, {["ranch"] = 0.5}, false)
	}
	
	local RanchProductionScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, RanchProductionList)
	
	local NormalScoring =	
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 6*60),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {MaintainSomeCows, RanchProductionScoring})
	}
	
	local StartDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, StartOfGameScoring)
	local NormalDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, NormalScoring)
	
	-- scoring for late game
	local LateGameList =
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, CastleAgeScoring),
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 18, -1, true)
	}
	
	-- scoring for before castle age
	local MidGameList = {
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 9, -1, true),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, PreCastleAgeScoring)
	}
	
	local MidGameScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, MidGameList)
	local LateGameScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, LateGameList)
		
	result = {
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {StartDecisionBranch, NormalDecisionBranch}),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {MidGameScoring, LateGameScoring})
	}
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_ExpansionTC(aiPlayer)
	
	function typicalPurposeWeight(aiplayer, pbg)
	   return 0.1
	end
	
	
	local expansionDecisionList = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, typicalPurposeWeight),
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true)
	}

	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		-- Typically Expansion TCs  placement style 'ExpansionBase' makes them build at
		-- suitable expansion sites (good resources). This in turn causes PlannedPlacementScore to
		-- modulate how many TCs we build.
		-- However all mongol structures use the build style 'NearBlueprint' which causes them
		-- to build near the ovoo. With this in mind PlannedPlacementScore will always be positive
		-- causing the Mongol AIPlayer to spam TCs. Therfore we must limit mongol TCs

		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true)
	else
		-- don't build more than 4 TCs. 3 + capital
		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	end
	
	local expansionDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,expansionDecisionList)
	
	local twoTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, TwoTCDesire),

		-- 1 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 2 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, 2, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local threeTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, ThreeTCDesire),

		-- 2 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 3 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, 3, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local islandDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_IslandNeedingExpansionBase(aiPlayer)
	
	-- We consider both possibilities and chose the max score
	local branchingDecisions = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		twoTCDesireBranch,
		threeTCDesireBranch,
		expansionDecisionBranch,
		islandDecisionBranch
	})
	
	local result =  
	{
		branchingDecisions,
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, 0.3),
	}
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_DropOffs(aiPlayer)
	-- failsafe case makes the score for this dropoff very high if we have not recently 
	-- built a dropoff of this type AND the resource is fundamental (needed for building the dropoff) 
	-- AND we currently have very little of the resource
	local failsafe = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),
			
			-- returns a value between 0 and 1
			AIProductionScoring_AmountOfResourceNeeded(aiPlayer, 25.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_LowResourceIncome(aiPlayer, 4.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_IsProductionBlockedByThisResource(aiPlayer)
		})
	
	local normalDropoffScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			
			-- Do I need more drop offs go get the resources that I need/want (faster)?
			-- This is what drives the decision most of the time.
			-- 0 as long as we don't need the drop off at all.
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),

			-- When produced, pause production for some time, to let various parts of the AI react to the new drop off.
			-- Should not be too short because villagers need to walk to the construction site and build it before
			-- any of the other parts of AI (like ScarcityAndDeficiency) can update to the new dropoff being there.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 50.0),

			-- Return 0.0 if placement score is invalid, otherwise return 1.0, elephants should not come through this path
			AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScoreValid(aiPlayer),

			-- As of writing this comment we never drop economy all the way to 0 so this is just used to help order
			-- the queue based on strategic intention.
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		})
	
	-- if villagers run out of things to gather on colonized island it's better to try and build a dropoff then stand around doing nothing
	-- returns 0 or 1
	local villagersRunOutOfThingToGather = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
		{
			-- This is here because we can't figure out why the AI is sometimes going ham with lumber camps.
			-- At the time of adding this comment both other options have NotProducedRecently for at least 60s in the
			-- scoring, yet the AI can sometimes get into a bugged state where it is spamming down lumber camps in a
			-- 20 second interval. So the NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland probably has some edge
			-- case bug and can't be trusted. I'm forcing a 3 minute delay on this for the following reasons:
			-- 1. We don't have a good way to reproduce this bug.
			-- 2. This branch is meant to deal with naval maps where the AI colonizes new islands and needs to build
			--    drop-offs there. Naval AI has been de-prioritized and is less important than land features.
			--    This interferes with gameplay on land.
			-- 3. The worst case on a naval map would be that the AI just build a drop off before setting foot on a new
			--    island and has to wait for 3 minutes. But that is only the case if the normal drop off scoring branch
			--    doesn't trigger. If the normal scoring doesn't trigger then the AI doesn't need wood right now so no
			--    big loss. Just some idle villagers in edge case situations of a non-priority feature (naval).
			--    In contrast our current bad case is that the AI wastes all of it's wood in plastering the entire area
			--    in and around a forest with lumber camps. It wastes a lot of wood and wastes villager time by
			--    dedicating one to building more and more lumber camps. And the community called it out a lot.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),

			AIProductionScoring_NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland(aiPlayer)
		})
		
	return 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {normalDropoffScoring, failsafe, villagersRunOutOfThingToGather})		
	}
end

function ScoringFunctions_Gatherer(aiPlayer)
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player)
	local villager_max_percentage = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_max_pop_percentage")
	local villager_production_delay_time = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_production_delay_time")  -- delay time between each villager queued up
	
	-- for naval maps, lower the max number of Villagers to make room for fishing boats
	if AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() and AI_AreThereAnyDeepwaterFish(aiPlayer) then
		if difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
		elseif difficulty == AID_HARD then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.05
		end
	end
	
	-- if super late into the game and higher difficulties, reduce the villagers to allow more room for traders and military 
	if World_GetGameTime() >= 60*40 and difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
		villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
	end
	
	local result = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_MultipleProduced(aiPlayer, 0.1),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxPopCapPercentage(aiPlayer, villager_max_percentage, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 3.0, 2.0, true, true)
	}
	
	-- if playing as Mongol or Golden Horde and higher difficulties
	if difficulty >= AID_HARD and Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		
		-- increase the production delay time to ensure that we have resources to age up to feudal age
		local DarkAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
			{
				AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, DarkAgeScoring),
				AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 55.5)
			})
		
		-- use default otherwise
		local feudal_age_list = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FeudalAgeScoring)
		}
		
		if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 then
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
		else
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 0.125)
		end
		
		local FeudalAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, feudal_age_list)
		
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {DarkAgeMinimumScoring, FeudalAgeMinimumScoring})
	end
	
	-- If the delay time is high enough, add the function to delay production.
	-- We need to check this because if the delay time is not greater than 0.125 seconds (one sim tick) then this scoring function throws an assert.  
	if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 and not Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") or AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "templar") then
		-- Templars use upgrades from the TC to age up, and this can be blocked by the villager production.
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NoUpgradeProductionBlockedByThisProduction(aiPlayer, "age_up_upgrade");
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_ExpansionTC(aiPlayer)
	
	function typicalPurposeWeight(aiplayer, pbg)
	   return 0.1
	end
	
	
	local expansionDecisionList = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, typicalPurposeWeight),
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true)
	}

	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		-- Typically Expansion TCs  placement style 'ExpansionBase' makes them build at
		-- suitable expansion sites (good resources). This in turn causes PlannedPlacementScore to
		-- modulate how many TCs we build.
		-- However all mongol structures use the build style 'NearBlueprint' which causes them
		-- to build near the ovoo. With this in mind PlannedPlacementScore will always be positive
		-- causing the Mongol AIPlayer to spam TCs. Therfore we must limit mongol TCs

		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true)
	else
		-- don't build more than 4 TCs. 3 + capital
		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	end
	
	local expansionDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,expansionDecisionList)
	
	local twoTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, TwoTCDesire),

		-- 1 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 2 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, 2, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local threeTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, ThreeTCDesire),

		-- 2 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 3 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, 3, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local islandDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_IslandNeedingExpansionBase(aiPlayer)
	
	-- We consider both possibilities and chose the max score
	local branchingDecisions = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		twoTCDesireBranch,
		threeTCDesireBranch,
		expansionDecisionBranch,
		islandDecisionBranch
	})
	
	local result =  
	{
		branchingDecisions,
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, 0.3),
	}
	
	return result
end

        local ok, t = pcall(World_GetGameTime)

        AIProductionScoring_PresenceOfMyTypes(aiPlayer, {ranch=0.5}, false),
    }
    local ranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, ranchList)
    local maintain = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
    local normalList = {

        AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {maintain, ranch}),
    }
    local startBr = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, startList)
    local normalBr = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, normalList)
    local lateList = {
        AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, CastleAgeScoring),

    local midList = {
        AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 9, -1, true),
        AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, PreCastleAgeScoring),
    }
    local mid = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, midList)

function ScoringFunctions_Cattle(aiPlayer)
	-- At the start of the game we want an early cow, then we only want a few until we start having ranches to fill. As we get more ranches, then we increase cattle production.
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	
	-- this scoring function returns 0 if the game time is past a minimum duration
	function FirstCattleScoring(aiplayer) 
		if World_GetGameTime() < 6*60 then	
			return 0.0
		else
			return 1000.0
		end
	end
	
	-- scoring for the first cattle to produce at start of game
	local StartOfGameScoring = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FirstCattleScoring)
	}
	
	-- Scoring for low production of cows
	local MaintainSomeCows = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	
	-- Scoring for high production of cows. Requires a mill to prevent choking the town center villager production.
	local RanchProductionList =
	{
		AIProductionScoring_PresenceOfMyTypes(aiPlayer, {["villager"] = 0.01}, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PresenceOfMyTypes(aiPlayer, {["ranch"] = 0.5}, false)
	}
	
	local RanchProductionScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, RanchProductionList)
	
	local NormalScoring =	
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MinimumGameTime(aiPlayer, 6*60),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {MaintainSomeCows, RanchProductionScoring})
	}
	
	local StartDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, StartOfGameScoring)
	local NormalDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, NormalScoring)
	
	-- scoring for late game
	local LateGameList =
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, CastleAgeScoring),
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 18, -1, true)
	}
	
	-- scoring for before castle age
	local MidGameList = {
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 9, -1, true),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, PreCastleAgeScoring)
	}
	
	local MidGameScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, MidGameList)
	local LateGameScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, LateGameList)
		
	result = {
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {StartDecisionBranch, NormalDecisionBranch}),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {MidGameScoring, LateGameScoring})
	}
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_DropOffs(aiPlayer)
	-- failsafe case makes the score for this dropoff very high if we have not recently 
	-- built a dropoff of this type AND the resource is fundamental (needed for building the dropoff) 
	-- AND we currently have very little of the resource
	local failsafe = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),
			
			-- returns a value between 0 and 1
			AIProductionScoring_AmountOfResourceNeeded(aiPlayer, 25.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_LowResourceIncome(aiPlayer, 4.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_IsProductionBlockedByThisResource(aiPlayer)
		})
	
	local normalDropoffScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			
			-- Do I need more drop offs go get the resources that I need/want (faster)?
			-- This is what drives the decision most of the time.
			-- 0 as long as we don't need the drop off at all.
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),

			-- When produced, pause production for some time, to let various parts of the AI react to the new drop off.
			-- Should not be too short because villagers need to walk to the construction site and build it before
			-- any of the other parts of AI (like ScarcityAndDeficiency) can update to the new dropoff being there.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 50.0),

			-- Return 0.0 if placement score is invalid, otherwise return 1.0, elephants should not come through this path
			AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScoreValid(aiPlayer),

			-- As of writing this comment we never drop economy all the way to 0 so this is just used to help order
			-- the queue based on strategic intention.
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		})
	
	-- if villagers run out of things to gather on colonized island it's better to try and build a dropoff then stand around doing nothing
	-- returns 0 or 1
	local villagersRunOutOfThingToGather = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
		{
			-- This is here because we can't figure out why the AI is sometimes going ham with lumber camps.
			-- At the time of adding this comment both other options have NotProducedRecently for at least 60s in the
			-- scoring, yet the AI can sometimes get into a bugged state where it is spamming down lumber camps in a
			-- 20 second interval. So the NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland probably has some edge
			-- case bug and can't be trusted. I'm forcing a 3 minute delay on this for the following reasons:
			-- 1. We don't have a good way to reproduce this bug.
			-- 2. This branch is meant to deal with naval maps where the AI colonizes new islands and needs to build
			--    drop-offs there. Naval AI has been de-prioritized and is less important than land features.
			--    This interferes with gameplay on land.
			-- 3. The worst case on a naval map would be that the AI just build a drop off before setting foot on a new
			--    island and has to wait for 3 minutes. But that is only the case if the normal drop off scoring branch
			--    doesn't trigger. If the normal scoring doesn't trigger then the AI doesn't need wood right now so no
			--    big loss. Just some idle villagers in edge case situations of a non-priority feature (naval).
			--    In contrast our current bad case is that the AI wastes all of it's wood in plastering the entire area
			--    in and around a forest with lumber camps. It wastes a lot of wood and wastes villager time by
			--    dedicating one to building more and more lumber camps. And the community called it out a lot.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),

			AIProductionScoring_NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland(aiPlayer)
		})
		
	return 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {normalDropoffScoring, failsafe, villagersRunOutOfThingToGather})		
	}
end

function ScoringFunctions_MilitaryProductionBuilding(aiPlayer)
	-- Buildings that produce military units or upgrades
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player) 
	local groupUtility = function(aiPlayer, pbg, prodGroupID)
		local perPBGCurrentScale = 0.25
		local perPBGEverScale = 0
		local maxPBGsFromGroupCurrent = -1
		return GroupUtility(aiPlayer, prodGroupID, pbg, maxPBGsFromGroupCurrent, perPBGCurrentScale, perPBGEverScale)
	end

	local result =  
	{
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, -1.0),
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["combat"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_ProductionQueueContention(aiPlayer, 8, 20),
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, groupUtility),
		AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 10.0),
	}
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if difficulty <= AID_EASY then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, false)
	elseif difficulty == AID_NORMAL then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, -1, false)
	elseif difficulty >= AID_HARD then 
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, false)
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_Gatherer(aiPlayer)
	local player = AI_ConvertToSimPlayer(aiPlayer)
	local difficulty = AI_GetDifficulty(player)
	local villager_max_percentage = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_max_pop_percentage")
	local villager_production_delay_time = AIPlayer_GetStateModelFloat(aiPlayer, "ai_difficulty_villager_production_delay_time")  -- delay time between each villager queued up
	
	-- for naval maps, lower the max number of Villagers to make room for fishing boats
	if AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() and AI_AreThereAnyDeepwaterFish(aiPlayer) then
		if difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
		elseif difficulty == AID_HARD then
			villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.05
		end
	end
	
	-- if super late into the game and higher difficulties, reduce the villagers to allow more room for traders and military 
	if World_GetGameTime() >= 60*40 and difficulty >= AID_EXPERT then
		villager_max_percentage = villager_max_percentage - 0.1
	end
	
	local result = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true),
		AIProductionScoring_MultipleProduced(aiPlayer, 0.1),
		AIProductionScoring_MaxPopCapPercentage(aiPlayer, villager_max_percentage, true),
		AIProductionScoring_PopulationPercentage(aiPlayer, 3.0, 2.0, true, true)
	}
	
	-- if playing as Mongol or Golden Horde and higher difficulties
	if difficulty >= AID_HARD and Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		
		-- increase the production delay time to ensure that we have resources to age up to feudal age
		local DarkAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
			{
				AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, DarkAgeScoring),
				AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 55.5)
			})
		
		-- use default otherwise
		local feudal_age_list = 
		{
			AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, FeudalAgeScoring)
		}
		
		if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 then
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
		else
			feudal_age_list[#feudal_age_list + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 0.125)
		end
		
		local FeudalAgeMinimumScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, feudal_age_list)
		
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {DarkAgeMinimumScoring, FeudalAgeMinimumScoring})
	end
	
	-- If the delay time is high enough, add the function to delay production.
	-- We need to check this because if the delay time is not greater than 0.125 seconds (one sim tick) then this scoring function throws an assert.  
	if villager_production_delay_time > 0.125 and not Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol_ha_gol") then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, villager_production_delay_time)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") or AI_ArePlayersOnDifferentIslands() then
		result[#result +1 ] = AIProductionScoring_RemainingPersonnelPopCap(aiPlayer, 10)
	end
	
	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "templar") then
		-- Templars use upgrades from the TC to age up, and this can be blocked by the villager production.
		result[#result + 1] = AIProductionScoring_NoUpgradeProductionBlockedByThisProduction(aiPlayer, "age_up_upgrade");
	end
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_ExpansionTC(aiPlayer)
	
	function typicalPurposeWeight(aiplayer, pbg)
	   return 0.1
	end
	
	
	local expansionDecisionList = 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, typicalPurposeWeight),
		AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true)
	}

	if Util_IsPlayerRace(aiPlayer, "mongol") then
		-- Typically Expansion TCs  placement style 'ExpansionBase' makes them build at
		-- suitable expansion sites (good resources). This in turn causes PlannedPlacementScore to
		-- modulate how many TCs we build.
		-- However all mongol structures use the build style 'NearBlueprint' which causes them
		-- to build near the ovoo. With this in mind PlannedPlacementScore will always be positive
		-- causing the Mongol AIPlayer to spam TCs. Therfore we must limit mongol TCs

		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, -1, true)
	else
		-- don't build more than 4 TCs. 3 + capital
		expansionDecisionList[#expansionDecisionList + 1] = AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 3, -1, true)
	end
	
	local expansionDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,expansionDecisionList)
	
	local twoTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, TwoTCDesire),

		-- 1 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 2 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 1, 2, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local threeTCDesireBranch = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {
		AIProductionScoring_LuaScoringFunction(aiPlayer, ThreeTCDesire),

		-- 2 extra TC, capital is a different blueprint
		-- build a total of 3 only, so if 1 gets destroyed it can get rebuild but don't try to do it over and over
		AIProductionScoring_UnderCountLimit(aiPlayer, 2, 3, true),

		-- always score it, so the AI has a need for stone and it starts to prioritize the TC sooner.
		-- This should make the AI build it early for a "booming" playstyle
		AIProductionScoring_ClampedScoringFunction(
			aiPlayer, 0.75, 1.0, AIProductionScoring_TimeToAcquire(aiPlayer, 300.0, true, false, true))
	})

	local islandDecisionBranch = AIProductionScoring_IslandNeedingExpansionBase(aiPlayer)
	
	-- We consider both possibilities and chose the max score
	local branchingDecisions = AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
	{
		twoTCDesireBranch,
		threeTCDesireBranch,
		expansionDecisionBranch,
		islandDecisionBranch
	})
	
	local result =  
	{
		branchingDecisions,
		AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScore(aiPlayer, 0.3),
	}
	
	return result
end

function ScoringFunctions_DropOffs(aiPlayer)
	-- failsafe case makes the score for this dropoff very high if we have not recently 
	-- built a dropoff of this type AND the resource is fundamental (needed for building the dropoff) 
	-- AND we currently have very little of the resource
	local failsafe = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),
			
			-- returns a value between 0 and 1
			AIProductionScoring_AmountOfResourceNeeded(aiPlayer, 25.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_LowResourceIncome(aiPlayer, 4.0),
			
			-- returns 0 or 1
			AIProductionScoring_IsProductionBlockedByThisResource(aiPlayer)
		})
	
	local normalDropoffScoring = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer, 
		{
			
			-- Do I need more drop offs go get the resources that I need/want (faster)?
			-- This is what drives the decision most of the time.
			-- 0 as long as we don't need the drop off at all.
			AIProductionScoring_ScarcityAndDeficiencyScore(aiPlayer),

			-- When produced, pause production for some time, to let various parts of the AI react to the new drop off.
			-- Should not be too short because villagers need to walk to the construction site and build it before
			-- any of the other parts of AI (like ScarcityAndDeficiency) can update to the new dropoff being there.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 50.0),

			-- Return 0.0 if placement score is invalid, otherwise return 1.0, elephants should not come through this path
			AIProductionScoring_PlannedPlacementScoreValid(aiPlayer),

			-- As of writing this comment we never drop economy all the way to 0 so this is just used to help order
			-- the queue based on strategic intention.
			AIProductionScoring_StrategicIntention(aiPlayer, { ["economy"] = 1.0}),
		})
	
	-- if villagers run out of things to gather on colonized island it's better to try and build a dropoff then stand around doing nothing
	-- returns 0 or 1
	local villagersRunOutOfThingToGather = AIProductionScoring_MultiplyListScoringFunction(aiPlayer,
		{
			-- This is here because we can't figure out why the AI is sometimes going ham with lumber camps.
			-- At the time of adding this comment both other options have NotProducedRecently for at least 60s in the
			-- scoring, yet the AI can sometimes get into a bugged state where it is spamming down lumber camps in a
			-- 20 second interval. So the NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland probably has some edge
			-- case bug and can't be trusted. I'm forcing a 3 minute delay on this for the following reasons:
			-- 1. We don't have a good way to reproduce this bug.
			-- 2. This branch is meant to deal with naval maps where the AI colonizes new islands and needs to build
			--    drop-offs there. Naval AI has been de-prioritized and is less important than land features.
			--    This interferes with gameplay on land.
			-- 3. The worst case on a naval map would be that the AI just build a drop off before setting foot on a new
			--    island and has to wait for 3 minutes. But that is only the case if the normal drop off scoring branch
			--    doesn't trigger. If the normal scoring doesn't trigger then the AI doesn't need wood right now so no
			--    big loss. Just some idle villagers in edge case situations of a non-priority feature (naval).
			--    In contrast our current bad case is that the AI wastes all of it's wood in plastering the entire area
			--    in and around a forest with lumber camps. It wastes a lot of wood and wastes villager time by
			--    dedicating one to building more and more lumber camps. And the community called it out a lot.
			AIProductionScoring_NotProducedRecently(aiPlayer, 180.0),

			AIProductionScoring_NoAvailableNearbyDepositsLeftOnColonizedIsland(aiPlayer)
		})
		
	return 
	{
		AIProductionScoring_MaxScoringFunction(aiPlayer, {normalDropoffScoring, failsafe, villagersRunOutOfThingToGather})		
	}
end
